newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timah gets nod for gold exploration.
newsitem.headline: Timah gets nod for gold exploration.

text.p: Indonesia's state-controlled PT Tambang Timah, the world's largest integrated tin miner, said on Tuesday it had government approval to explore for gold deposits in Sumatra, Kalimantan and East Java.

"The government agreed in principle late last year to allow us to explore for gold along the southern coast of East Java. This has brought our gold exploration areas to around seven so far," corporate secretary Prasetyo B. Saksono told Reuters.
Saksono said Timah, also listed in London, had the right to explore for gold in five areas in Kalimantan on Borneo island and one area in North Sumatra.
Saksono declined to give details on the exploration work, saying the firm allocated around five billion rupiah annually for exploration. It has not so far produced any gold.
He said Timah had also expressed interest to having a stake in one of the world's richest gold find in Busang, Kalimantan.

The government has given Canadian miners Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp to mid-February to reach agreements with their Indonesian partners before getting the go-ahead to further explore and develop Busang.
Bre-X estimates the Busang find contains over 57 million ounces of gold.
Placer Dome Inc is among other firms who have expressed an interest in Busang.

Saksono denied a report on Tuesday in the Republika daily newspaper that Timah unit PT Timah Investasi Mineral had approached President Suharto's second daughter Siti Hediati Prabowo to set up an alliance to seek an interest in Busang.
Barrick already has an association with a company controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.
